        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
```javascript
  }
}

```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
```
    }
  }
}


        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
```javascript
  }
}

```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
  }
}


print(f"Space LongName: {space.LongName}")

    print(f"  {pset_name}:")
    for key, val in props.items():
        if 'Area' in key or 'Volume' in key:

            elem_type = rel.RelatedBuildingElement.is_a()
            elem_name = rel.RelatedBuildingElement.Name
            elem_guid = rel.RelatedBuildingElement.GlobalId
            print(f"  Element: {elem_type}, Name: {elem_name}, GUID: {elem_guid}")

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
```javascript
  }
}
```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
```
    }
  }
}


```python
import ifcopenshell.api.spatial
```

### Assign IFC Elements to Spatial Containers

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Demonstrates assigning IFC elements (like IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcDoor) to spatial containers (e.g., IfcBuildingStorey) using `ifcopenshell.api.spatial`. It covers placing elements, moving them between containers, and retrieving an element's container. Requires `ifcopenshell.api.root` and `ifcopenshell.util.element`.

```python
import ifcopenshell.api.spatial
import ifcopenshell.util.element

# Assuming 'model' and 'storey' are defined
# model = ifcopenshell.file()

# storey2 = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBuildingStorey", name="Level 02")

# Create elements
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
slab = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcSlab")
door = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcDoor")

# Place elements in storey
ifcopenshell.api.spatial.assign_container(
    model,
    relating_structure=storey,
    products=[wall, slab, door]
)

ifcopenshell.api.spatial.assign_container(
    model,
    relating_structure=storey2,
    products=[door]
)

print(f"Wall is in: {container.Name}")  # "Level 01"
```

### Find Spatial Container of an Element in IFC Model with IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/code_examples.rst

This code snippet illustrates how to find the immediate spatial container (e.g., storey, space) of a given IFC element using `ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container`. It assumes an IFC model is loaded and an 'IfcWall' instance is available.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element

model = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')

wall = model.by_type("IfcWall")[0]
# Walls are typically located on a storey, equipment might be located in spaces, etc
container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
# The wall is located on Level 01
print(f"The wall is located on {container.Name}")
```

### Extract Wall Properties and Quantities with IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/code_examples.rst

Demonstrates how to retrieve property sets (Psets) and quantities for wall elements in an IFC model. It shows how to get all Psets and quantities, or filter for only properties or only quantities using `ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets`. Assumes an IFC model is loaded.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element

model = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')

wall = model.by_type("IfcWall")[0]
wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

# Get all properties and quantities as a dictionary
# returns {"Pset_WallCommon": {"id": 123, "FireRating": "2HR", ...}}
psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall_type)
print(psets)

# Get all properties and quantities of the wall, including inherited type properties
psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
print(psets)

# Get only properties and not quantities
print(ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall, psets_only=True))

# Get only quantities and not properties
print(ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall, qtos_only=True))
```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
  }
}


### Get Door Occurrences by Type in IFC Model with IfcOpenShell

### Assign IFC Elements to Spatial Containers

Demonstrates assigning IFC elements (like IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcDoor) to spatial containers (e.g., IfcBuildingStorey) using `ifcopenshell.api.spatial`. It covers placing elements, moving them between containers, and retrieving an element's container. Requires `ifcopenshell.api.root` and `ifcopenshell.util.element`.

```python
import ifcopenshell.api.spatial

# model = ifcopenshell.file()

slab = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcSlab")

ifcopenshell.api.spatial.assign_container(
    model,
    relating_structure=storey,
    products=[wall, slab, door]
)

    model,
    relating_structure=storey2,
    products=[door]
)
```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
```javascript
  }
}

```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
```
    }
  }
}


```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element

# Walls are typically located on a storey, equipment might be located in spaces, etc

# The wall is located on Level 01
print(f"The wall is located on {container.Name}")
```

Demonstrates assigning IFC elements (like IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcDoor) to spatial containers (e.g., IfcBuildingStorey) using `ifcopenshell.api.spatial`.         ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
```javascript
  }
}

```

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
```
  }
}


import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from typing import List
import os

# Test the function implementation on all available models

def check_large_spaces_more_than_one_door(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check if large spaces (area >= 50) have at least 2 doors.
    
    Parameters:
    - Space Group Type: Is Undefined (no filtering)
    - Include Space Area: >= 50.0
    - Exclude - Space Usage: One Of [Outdoor Space, Parking, Terrace]
    - Target Value: 2 doors
    - Exclude door = Hatch
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule (large spaces with fewer than 2 doors)
    """

    violating_guids = []
    
    # Get all spaces

    if not spaces:

    # Get all IfcRelSpaceBoundary for door counting
    rel_boundaries = model.by_type('IfcRelSpaceBoundary')
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    spaces_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        name = getattr(space, 'LongName', None) or getattr(space, 'Name', '') or ''
        spaces_data.append({"guid": space.GlobalId, "name": name})
    
    # Classify spaces
    classified = classify_spaces(spaces_data, path_ifc_model)
    
    # Create mapping from guid to classification
    classification_map = {c['guid']: c['classification'] for c in classified}
    
    # Excluded space usages
    excluded_usages = {'Outdoor Space', 'Parking', 'Terrace'}
    
    # Check each space
    for space in spaces:
        guid = space.GlobalId
        
        # Check if space is in excluded usage
        if guid not in classification_map:
            continue
        classification = classification_map[guid]
        if classification in excluded_usages:
            continue
        
        # Get space area
        psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(space)
        area = None
        for pset_name, props in psets.items():
            if 'Area' in props:
                area_val = props['Area']
                if isinstance(area_val, (int, float)) and area_val >= 50.0:
                    area = area_val
                    break
        
        # Only check spaces with area >= 50
        if area is None:

        # Count doors (excluding hatch doors)
        door_count = 0
        for rel in rel_boundaries:

                    if not is_hatch:
                        door_count += 1
        
        # Check if space has less than 2 doors
        if door_count < 2:
            violating_guids.append(guid)

        ### Handle Mouse Click for IFC Model Interaction with IFC.js

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/pyodide/demo-app/index.html

This function processes mouse click events to enable interactive editing of the IFC model. Depending on the `mouseMode`, it allows users to draw walls by defining two points, or to place doors and windows at selected locations. It utilizes `getPoint` to determine click coordinates and `createShape` to add new elements to the model. It also includes logic to remove existing elements before adding new ones, ensuring a clean update.

```javascript
function onMouseClick(event) {
  let newPoint = getPoint(event);
  if (mouseMode == 1) {
    if (previousPoint != null) {
      createShape(modelObject.create_2pt_wall([previousPoint.x, previousPoint.y], [newPoint.x, newPoint.y], 0, 3., 0.2, modelObject.storey));
    }
    previousPoint = newPoint;
  }
  if (mouseMode == 2 || mouseMode == 3) {
    if (newPoint !== null) {
      let { point, object } = newPoint;
      const guid = objectMapping[object.uuid];
      const toRemove = []
      scene.traverse((obj) => {
        if (objectMapping[obj.uuid] == guid) {
          toRemove.push(obj);
        }
      });
      toRemove.forEach(obj => obj.removeFromParent());
      createShape(modelObject.create_fill(mouseMode == 2 ? 'door' : 'window', [point.x, point.y, point.z], guid));
      createShape(modelObject.get_element(guid));
    }
  }
}

```

    """
    Check if large spaces (area >= 50) have at least 2 doors.
    
    Parameters:
    - Space Group Type: Is Undefined (no filtering)
    - Include Space Area: >= 50.0
    - Exclude - Space Usage: One Of [Outdoor Space, Parking, Terrace]
    - Target Value: 2 doors
    - Exclude door = Hatch
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule (large spaces with fewer than 2 doors)
    """
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    violating_guids = []
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Get all IfcRelSpaceBoundary for door counting
    rel_boundaries = model.by_type('IfcRelSpaceBoundary')
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    spaces_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        name = getattr(space, 'LongName', None) or getattr(space, 'Name', '') or ''
        spaces_data.append({"guid": space.GlobalId, "name": name})
    
    # Classify spaces
    classified = classify_spaces(spaces_data, path_ifc_model)
    
    # Create mapping from guid to classification
    classification_map = {c['guid']: c['classification'] for c in classified}
    
    # Excluded space usages
    excluded_usages = {'Outdoor Space', 'Parking', 'Terrace'}
    
    # Check each space
    for space in spaces:
        guid = space.GlobalId
        
        # Check if space is in excluded usage
        if guid not in classification_map:
            continue
        classification = classification_map[guid]
        if classification in excluded_usages:

        # Get space area
        psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(space)
        area = None
        for pset_name, props in psets.items():
            if 'Area' in props:
                area_val = props['Area']
                if isinstance(area_val, (int, float)) and area_val >= 50.0:
                    area = area_val
                    break
        
        # Only check spaces with area >= 50
        if area is None:
            continue
        
        # Count doors (excluding hatch doors)
        door_count = 0
        for rel in rel_boundaries:
            if rel.RelatingSpace and rel.RelatingSpace.GlobalId == guid:
                if rel.RelatedBuildingElement and 'Door' in rel.RelatedBuildingElement.is_a():
                    door = rel.RelatedBuildingElement

                    door_name = getattr(door, 'Name', '')
                    if door_name and 'Hatch' in door_name:

                    if not is_hatch:
                        door_count += 1
        
        # Check if space has less than 2 doors
        if door_count < 2:
            violating_guids.append(guid)
    
    return violating_guids

import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from typing import List
import os


def check_large_spaces_more_than_one_door(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check if large spaces (area >= 50) have at least 2 doors.
    
    Rule Parameters:
    - Include Space Group Type: Is Undefined (no filtering)
    - Include Space Area: >= 50.0
    - Exclude - Space Usage: One Of [Outdoor Space, Parking, Terrace]
    - Target Value: 2 doors minimum
    - Exclude door = Hatch
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule
        (large spaces with fewer than 2 non-hatch doors)
        
    Example:
        >>> guids = check_large_spaces_more_than_one_door('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(guids)} violations")
    """
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    violating_guids: List[str] = []
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Get all IfcRelSpaceBoundary for door counting
    rel_boundaries = model.by_type('IfcRelSpaceBoundary')
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    spaces_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        name = getattr(space, 'LongName', None) or getattr(space, 'Name', '') or ''
        spaces_data.append({"guid": space.GlobalId, "name": name})
    
    # Classify spaces
    classified = classify_spaces(spaces_data, path_ifc_model)
    
    # Create mapping from guid to classification
    classification_map = {c['guid']: c['classification'] for c in classified}
    
    # Excluded space usages
    excluded_usages = {'Outdoor Space', 'Parking', 'Terrace'}
    
    # Check each space
    for space in spaces:
        guid = space.GlobalId
        
        # Check if space is in excluded usage
        if guid not in classification_map:
            continue
        classification = classification_map[guid]
        if classification in excluded_usages:
            continue
        
        # Get space area
        psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(space)
        area = None
        for pset_name, props in psets.items():
            if 'Area' in props:
                area_val = props['Area']
                if isinstance(area_val, (int, float)) and area_val >= 50.0:
                    area = area_val
                    break
        
        # Only check spaces with area >= 50
        if area is None:
            continue
        
        # Count doors (excluding hatch doors)
        door_count = 0
        for rel in rel_boundaries:
            if rel.RelatingSpace and rel.RelatingSpace.GlobalId == guid:
                if rel.RelatedBuildingElement and 'Door' in rel.RelatedBuildingElement.is_a():
                    door = rel.RelatedBuildingElement
                    
                    # Check if door is a hatch door (exclude)
                    is_hatch = False
                    door_name = getattr(door, 'Name', '')
                    if door_name and 'Hatch' in door_name:
                        is_hatch = True
                    
                    # Also check door properties for 'Hatch'
                    if not is_hatch:
                        door_psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(door)
                        for pset_name, props in door_psets.items():
                            for key, val in props.items():
                                if isinstance(val, str) and 'Hatch' in val:
                                    is_hatch = True
                                    break
                            if is_hatch:
                                break
                    
                    if not is_hatch:
                        door_count += 1
        
        # Check if space has less than 2 doors
        if door_count < 2:
            violating_guids.append(guid)
    
    return violating_guids
